supplier_excerpts.excerpt:
A supplied finite-dimensional truncated RG datum for this scheme
is an open set $\Omega\subset I\times\mathbb R^{2N}$ and a supplied
continuous map $\beta:\Omega\to\mathbb R^{2N}$. A truncated RG trajectory is
a continuously differentiable curve $C:I'\to\mathbb C^N$, on an interval
$I'\subset I$ for which $(t,\rho_N(C(t)))\in\Omega$, satisfying
$$\frac{d}{dt}\rho_N(C(t))=\beta(t,\rho_N(C(t))).$$
The components of $\beta$ are the beta functions under this logarithmic-scale
convention. If the supplied flow is complex-linear, with a supplied matrix
function $\Gamma:I'\to\mathbb C^{N\times N}$, its equation can be written
$C'=\Gamma(t)C$, where the real-coordinate vector field is
$\beta(t,\rho_N(C))=\rho_N(\Gamma(t)C)$. In this column-vector convention,
$\Gamma$ is called the anomalous-dimension matrix. A scheme record does not
assert that its coefficient-coordinate maps solve a supplied RG equation; that
relation, the entries of $\beta$, and any matching map are separate inputs.
This definition calculates no QFT beta function and supplies no bound on
omitted perturbative or higher-dimension terms.

A supplied finite-dimensional truncated RG datum for this scheme
is an open set $\Omega\subset I\times\mathbb R^{2N}$ and a supplied
continuous map $\beta:\Omega\to\mathbb R^{2N}$. A truncated RG trajectory is
a continuously differentiable curve $C:I'\to\mathbb C^N$, on an interval
$I'\subset I$ for which $(t,\rho_N(C(t)))\in\Omega$, satisfying
$$\frac{d}{dt}\rho_N(C(t))=\beta(t,\rho_N(C(t))).$$
The components of $\beta$ are the beta functions under this logarithmic-scale
convention. If the supplied flow is complex-linear, with a supplied matrix
function $\Gamma:I'\to\mathbb C^{N\times N}$, its equation can be written
$C'=\Gamma(t)C$, where the real-coordinate vector field is
$\beta(t,\rho_N(C))=\rho_N(\Gamma(t)C)$. In this column-vector convention,
$\Gamma$ is called the anomalous-dimension matrix. A scheme record does not
assert that its coefficient-coordinate maps solve a supplied RG equation; that
relation, the entries of $\beta$, and any matching map are separate inputs.
This definition calculates no QFT beta function and supplies no bound on
omitted perturbative or higher-dimension terms.

A declared matching calculation supplies a finite list of renormalized amplitudes or Green-function values $A_{\sigma,j}(t,c;\lambda_{\mathrm{IR}})$, where $j$ indexes the selected external states and kinematics, $c$ is a coefficient vector, and $\lambda_{\mathrm{IR}}$ denotes the common infrared regulator used in both descriptions. Let $U_\sigma\subset\mathbb C^{N_\sigma}$ be open coefficient domains for $\sigma\in\{+,-\}$. The supplied matching family is a jointly continuously differentiable real map $\widehat{\mathcal M}:\mathcal V\to\rho_{N_-}(U_-)$ on an open domain $\mathcal V\subset J\times\rho_{N_+}(U_+)$. Its admissible domain is the open subset $\mathcal U=\{(t,x)\in\mathcal V:(t,x)\in\Omega_+,\ (t,\widehat{\mathcal M}(t,x))\in\Omega_-\}$. It defines $M_t(c):=\rho_{N_-}^{-1}(\widehat{\mathcal M}(t,\rho_{N_+}(c)))$ for each admitted $(t,c)$, and $\widehat M_t(x):=\widehat{\mathcal M}(t,x)$ on the corresponding slice. Thus the scale derivative and coefficient derivative in the compatibility condition below both exist and are continuous. It is a matching map through the declared loop order, operator dimension, and mass-expansion order when, for every selected $j$ and every admitted pair $(t,c)$ with $c\in U_+$, the prescribed truncations of $A_{+,j}(t,c;\lambda_{\mathrm{IR}})$ and $A_{-,j}(t,M_t(c);\lambda_{\mathrm{IR}})$ agree. The truncation projection and its retained orders are part of the datum. This equality records only the selected amplitudes and orders; it neither estimates discarded terms nor asserts that a matching calculation exists for every model.

A matching map is RG-compatible on these domains when, in realified coefficient coordinates,
$$\partial_t\widehat M_t(x)+D_x\widehat M_t(x)\,\beta_+(t,x)=\beta_-\!\left(t,\widehat M_t(x)\right)$$
for every admitted $(t,x)$. Here $D_x$ is the ordinary real derivative with respect to the coefficient coordinates. RG-compatibility is an additional condition to be checked from the supplied beta functions and matching calculation; it does not follow merely from defining $M_t$ by amplitude equality.

Any two solutions through the same initial data agree on every common interval
containing $t_0$. Here local well-posedness means local existence, uniqueness,
and this uniform continuous dependence on initial coefficient data. Under
$C=\rho_N^{-1}(x)$, realified solutions give complex coefficient trajectories.
The theorem asserts no global solution, no bound on omitted terms, and no
calculation of a QFT beta function.

derivations.claim: The chain rule and the RG-compatibility identity show that the matched image of the high-energy trajectory solves the low-energy beta equation on the common interval.
For any matching scale s, the evolved low-energy solution and the transported high-energy trajectory have the same initial value; common-interval uniqueness identifies them.
At the same final scale, identical low-energy coefficient vectors and identical external, regulator, and truncation data give the same selected amplitude or Green-function value.
Finite induction applies the one-threshold uniqueness argument to the ordered composition of compatible matching maps and evolution flows.

pthm-aqft-matching-and-running-scale-ind.finite_checks_disposition: The conclusion is for arbitrary supplied locally Lipschitz vector fields and compatible differentiable maps; no finite numerical check replaces the chain-rule and uniqueness proof.
